abduction.def:
Movement of a limb or body part away from the midline.
Opposite: {{adduction|linktitle}}.

adduction.def:
Movement of a limb or body part toward the midline.
Opposite: {{abduction|linktitle}}.

extension.def:
Increases the angle between two bones, moving a segment away from the neutral position.
Opposite: {{flexion|linktitle}}.

epicondyle.def: A bony prominence on the distal end of a long bone, typically serving as an attachment point for muscles and ligaments.

flexion.def:
Decreases the angle between two bones in the {{sagittal|linkinternal}} plane (for example, bending the elbow).
Opposite: {{extension|linktitle}}.

fossa.def: A hollow or depression in the surface of a bone.

insertion.def: The part of a muscle that moves when the muscle contracts. See Muscle Origin and Insertion.

ligament.def: Strong tissue that connects bone to bone.

origin.def:
The part of a muscle that stays in place when the muscle contracts.
See Muscle Origin and Insertion.

sagittal.def: An anatomical plane running front to back, dividing the body into left and right sections.

tendon.def: Strong tissue that connects muscle to bone.

ventral.def: Near or on the belly side.
